# E23 build plan

Planning handoff for independent review, not authorization to bypass unresolved seams. The frozen design stays unchanged. Each coder receives its complete `tasks.json` entry. Shared rules and Part A decisions win, followed by unresolved review findings. All implementation paths come from `docs/tdd/E23.md:1070`.

## Build order and connections

At inspection, `hub/`, `ui/`, `adapters/`, `eval/`, `packages/contracts-ts/`, `contracts/api/` and the three E23 runtime configuration documents are absent. Existing root tooling, contracts and configuration belong to pharmacy. E01 supplies the effective generated contracts, kernel, platform, composition root and hub toolchain; E02 supplies authenticated sessions, roster and authorization. Do not create replacements. Unit work uses their actual protocols and `kernel.testing` under SYSTEM 10; real-stack gates require their real implementations (`docs/SYSTEM.md:2388`).

| Task | Concern and ownership summary | Start condition |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Mission module, both E23 application contracts, mission configuration/tests | E01/E02 build prerequisites; agreed mission event exports |
| T2 | Pure sensor rules, sensor configuration and rule tests | E01 contracts/kernel |
| T3 | Sensor capture, storage, timers, HTTP and module registration | T1 contracts and T2 rules frozen |
| T4 | Habitat adapter member, schemas, parser/transport tests and temporary demo files | Generated contracts and agreed adapter clock/CLI bindings |
| T5 | Seven Habitat feature files and component tests | Generated TS client and E03 shell contracts |
| T6 | Four E23 scenario files, including browser acceptance | T1 through T5 and the real providers needed for each positive scenario |

Start T1, T2, T4 and T5 independently when their listed prerequisites exist. Pure T2 rule work needs no unresolved cross-module event representation; T1 owns that boundary. T1 publishes both mission and sensor application contracts first; T2 owns pure rules without a reverse port dependency. T3 waits for both tasks. Unit tests may use kernel fakes; they do not prove integration. T1 late-binds `ActivationParticipant` implemented by T3, avoiding a factory cycle. T1 emits `environment.activated` before publishing `EnvironmentActivated` and invokes that participant after synchronous handlers drain. T3 uses T2 rules and E01 isolation once per accepted reading in order. T4 posts through the same real ingest HTTP boundary for all origins. T5 renders served projections through E03 slots. T6 drives these paths and returns defects to the file owner.

Rechecked every existing `docs/build/*/tasks.json`, including manifests added during planning, and other designs' section 13. No task overlaps another epic. E02 owns identity, E03 shell/copy/Today, E21 shared harness and fixture, E24 warnings, E25 routines, E27 guidance, E29 link state. E23 owns neither their implementations nor their integration fixes. Recheck manifests immediately before dispatch. Exact file ownership, including tests, is in `tasks.json`; no directory-wide ownership is implied by the table.

## End-to-end proof

T6 uses `create_app(settings)` through real HTTP with temporary on-disk SQLite, actual configuration loading, identity, middleware, repositories, transactions and event delivery. Browser checks use Playwright against the running hub and actual crew app, inside the owned Python scenario files. No in-hub mocks, dependency overrides, direct database seeding or request interception. External optional processes may be absent or use documented fakes. Use E01's approved fault/clock controls; if unavailable, request them instead of monkeypatching the hub. E21's explicit demo fixture supplies initial state; the fenced E23 demo files cover only their documented temporary feed role.

| Scenario file | Required E23 proof and trace |
|---|---|
| `test_environment.py` | Confirmed activation only, one active record, concurrent CAS, policy pins, scheduled effective time, post-EVA/day boundary, late-event ordering and no old-place current readings. Exact transit to Mars V66; Moon demo D18/D31/D33. Verify real E25 cadence, E27 kit list/count recomputation for D31 and E29 planned-down/next-contact Habitat line for D33 when those positive clauses run. Covers R34, T001 to 016/044/046/061/064/067 to 069/073/078/082/086. |
| `test_sensors.py` | Actual replay ingestion, original dates and origin words, RR-1 and DosTel1 golden outputs, no personal exposure, instrument dose-rate label, independent channel/conflict handling, dust effects, limit provenance, trend/marks, acknowledgement versus fresh dwell and scratch configuration edits. Covers R35/R41/R42/R43, V55/V56/V58/V59/V72/V73/V75, D01/D16/D19 and T029/036 to 045/048 to 050/058/063/065/075 to 077/080/087/090. Includes both c1 ingest regressions with real E24 warning history. |
| `test_fallbacks.py` | Stop feeds, delete deadlines and stall dispatcher separately; sweep/read paths stay conservative, quiet warning and manual fallback persist. Stop model/devices/ground, fail link views, interrupt every command around commit, fill storage, jump clocks, corrupt releases, revoke grants, restart/restore and exercise replica cursors. Storm during sleep wakes everyone, retains vehicle procedure and never offers a vehicle alarm control. Covers charter 6 critical paths, V57/V58/V70, T018/019/047/051 to 057/060/066/070/072/079/081/083 to 085/088/089/091/092. |

All V and D IDs above are scenario markers, with E23's partial ownership explicit. V75 also checks the E23 effect/todo text edits and client scan; other epics own the responder-step portion. T6 preserves all 92 design test IDs through unit/integration/scenario collection. Hardware-only T062 runs separately with `uv run --project adapters/habitat pytest -c adapters/habitat/pyproject.toml -q adapters/habitat/tests/test_hardware.py -m hardware` and is reported not measured without a device. Independent source-checked expectations from CONTRACTS 20 and the conformance arithmetic remain fixed; test inputs use configuration. Never derive medical expected outcomes from the same document being tested or tune content to obtain a pass.

A capture-only R-E23-2 interim can pass its negative tests while every evaluated positive scenario remains blocked. Real E24/E25/E27/E29 are required for their positive clauses; fakes do not earn those passes. Missing criteria, source approval, required provider, test collection, tool or registration fails the corresponding gate. No skip/xfail or reduced assertion closes acceptance.

## Gates and hand-in

Each task runs its exact commands in `tasks.json`. Python rule/parser properties use 1,000 examples. T6 reruns the complete built E23 suite, verifies 95% domain/application branch coverage, full condition coverage and complexity at most 15 for critical functions, and the sensor mutation score at least 0.80. Hub and adapter lint/type/import gates are separate; UI uses pnpm. Engine contract validation remains the charter's separate `uv run python scripts/validate_contracts.py` command, not a substitute for hub validation. CI and independent build review remain required, maximum three build rounds (AGENTS 5).

Executed planning check: `.venv/bin/python -B scripts/design_lint.py docs/tdd/E23.md` returned exit 1 with five check-10 provider errors and five check-4 warnings. This matches c1 and R-E23-21; do not suppress them. JSON, exact ownership, dependency and punctuation checks are planning evidence only. Runtime, coverage, mutation, browser, hardware and CI gates have not run because implementation/toolchain prerequisites are absent.
